beats.intro: Lesson two. [[sub]]The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer: how science turned into the first global agreement on ozone.
beats.science: The story starts with science. [[paper]]In nineteen seventy-four, two chemists, Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland, published a warning. [[rise]]C F Cs, they showed, drift up to the stratosphere, [[release]]where sunlight breaks them apart and releases chlorine. [[predict]]Keep releasing C F Cs, they predicted, and stratospheric ozone will fall. [[measure]]Several countries began measuring the ozone layer, including over Antarctica. [[nobel]]In nineteen ninety-five, Molina, Rowland and a third scientist, Paul Crutzen, shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work.
beats.agenda: Governments soon took notice. [[wmo]]In nineteen seventy-five, the World Meteorological Organization, with funding from the U N Environment Programme, brought scientists together, and issued its first statement on ozone. [[unep]]That pushed U N E P's Governing Council to make ozone a high priority. [[plan]]In nineteen seventy-seven, an international meeting adopted a World Plan of Action on the ozone layer. [[research]]Its focus: research, and monitoring, coordinated across countries. [[bridge]]Science had put ozone firmly on the political agenda.
beats.interests: But a treaty was hard to agree. [[global]]Ozone loss affects every country, so a treaty would only work if it was global. And countries wanted different things. [[dev]]Developing countries feared that limits on these chemicals could hold back their industrial growth. [[ind]]Countries whose industries relied heavily on them, like those of the European Union, worried about the cost. [[doubt]]Some argued that the harm had not been proven yet. [[early]]And countries that had already cut their own C F C use, like the United States, Canada, Sweden and Norway, didn't want others to keep using them. [[table]]All of these interests had to meet at one table.
beats.q1: Quick check. Match each concern to the countries that held it.
beats.adopted: Negotiations began in nineteen eighty-two. [[adopt]]On the twenty-second of March, nineteen eighty-five, the Vienna Convention was adopted by consensus. [[force]]It entered into force on the twenty-second of September, nineteen eighty-eight. [[universal]]And in two thousand nine, every country in the world had joined it. [[first]]It was the first international environmental treaty ever to reach universal ratification.
beats.stages: Adopted and entered into force are not the same thing. A treaty passes through four stages. [[s1]]First, negotiation, usually launched by a mandate from a body such as U N E P or the U N General Assembly. [[s2]]Second, adoption: the text is finalised. [[s3]]Third, ratification: each state formally agrees to be bound. Acceptance and approval work the same way. [[s4]]Fourth, entry into force, on the terms the treaty sets, often once enough countries have ratified. [[vienna]]For the Vienna Convention, that was ninety days after the twentieth country ratified.
beats.q2: Quick check. At which stage does a country formally agree to be bound by a treaty?
beats.framework: So what does the Convention actually require? [[frame]]It is a framework convention. [[noctrl]]It sets no specific limits on ozone-depleting substances. [[general]]Instead, it creates a general duty to protect the ozone layer, and calls for appropriate measures: [[m1]]laws and administrative measures, [[m2]]cooperation on research and scientific assessment, [[m3]]sharing information, [[m4]]and developing and transferring technology. [[later]]The specific controls were left for a later protocol: the Montreal Protocol, in Lesson three.
beats.precaution: The Convention did something else that mattered. [[before]]It accepted that action was needed before there was firm proof of harm. [[scale]]On one side, uncertain science. On the other, the risk of serious damage that cannot be undone. [[tip]]Act first, rather than wait. [[principle]]This is the precautionary principle, or approach. [[rio]]In nineteen ninety-two it was written into Principle fifteen of the Rio Declaration: a lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason to postpone cost-effective measures. The Vienna Convention is an early sign of that idea in international environmental law.
beats.institutions: Finally, who runs the Convention? [[cop]]At the top is the Conference of the Parties, or COP, which brings together every party. It meets every three years to review how the Convention is being carried out, and to decide policies and rules. [[bureau]]Its Bureau, a President, three Vice-Presidents and a Rapporteur, works for the parties between meetings, reviewing the science. [[orm]]The Ozone Research Managers are government research managers and scientists. They meet six months before each COP, and send it their research recommendations. [[sec]]And the Ozone Secretariat, at U N E P headquarters in Nairobi, Kenya, organises the meetings and shares information, [[both]]for both the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Science came first: Molina and Rowland's warning in nineteen seventy-four led to research plans and meetings. [[w2]]The Vienna Convention was adopted in nineteen eighty-five, entered into force in nineteen eighty-eight, and reached every country in two thousand nine. [[w3]]As a framework, it sets a general duty to protect the ozone layer, not specific controls, and it acts before full proof: the precautionary approach. [[w4]]Its bodies are the Conference of the Parties, its Bureau, the Ozone Research Managers, and the Secretariat in Nairobi. [[end]]Now, a short practice.
